links.outcome: AI urgency triage under-triage and over-triage versus GP ratings
links.effect: 83.7% categorical agreement (κ 0.69); greater likelihood of over-triage, rarely under-triaging; no cases deemed non-urgent by AI later reclassified as emergencies by GPs.
links.quote: No cases deemed non-urgent by AI were later reclassified as emergencies by GPs.

links.outcome: Agreement of AI triage urgency scores with GP urgency ratings
links.effect: Spearman ρ=0.796; 83.7% categorical agreement across eight urgency levels (κ 0.69).
links.quote: There was a strong correlation between AI and GP urgency ratings (ρ=0.796,  p 0.001), with 83.7% categorical agreement across eight urgency levels (κ 0.69,  p 0.001).

unlisted_practices: Real-time benchmarking of AI triage urgency against consensus clinician judgement

screen.reason: Evaluated the real-world deployment performance of an AI triage tool (Visiba Triage) compared to GP urgency ratings and assessed clinician and patient perceptions, but did not test a specific safeguard or deployment practice variation.
